A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MultiRole-R1, with matching methods, experiments, and appendices A–F. Their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support a reliable comparison despite additions and repagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark evaluations, diversity analyses, ablations, and human ratings in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and additionally reports distinct-opinion counts and an entropy-regularized GRPO pilot.

M1.justification: The role-synthesis, self-consistency filtering, SFT, and diversity-shaped GRPO procedure is retained. v4 explicitly connects rewards to role-aware accuracy and diversity, clarifying behavior already represented in v2 Figure 1 and Section 4.4. No procedural change is established.

E1.justification: Both versions train on BBQ, GLOQA, and ETHICS and evaluate additionally on CALI, CSQA, GSM8K, and AIME 2024. Creative writing appears only as future work in v4, without new evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Section 6.2 adds an actually attempted entropy-regularized GRPO comparator, reporting early entropy collapse qualitatively. The comparator sets in the main benchmark table and AIME comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported human-rating protocol changes from 60 outputs in v2 to 60 per model, totaling 240, independently scored by three raters in v4. This revises the stated evaluation design without establishing that it was rerun. Retained benchmark test counts and SFT settings are unchanged; newly supplied GRPO settings and validation counts are disclosures.

E4.justification: New Table 3 examines distinct opinions across More Think, SFT, vanilla GRPO, and MultiRole-R1. Section 6.2 adds a limited training-stability comparison against entropy regularization. Existing role-count, filtering, and pass@5 analyses remain; Figure 5 redisplays previously tabulated subscores.

E5.justification: v2 Table 4 reports human-rating means and alignment scores without uncertainty. v4 Table 5 adds ± quantities described as inter-rater variance and identifies three independent raters. This adds uncertainty reporting, without establishing additional training runs or seeds.

E6.justification: v4 adds opinion counts, including GLOQA values of 2.07 for MultiRole-R1 versus 1.73 for SFT+GRPO, and reports entropy collapse around 70 steps. The Qwen-7B BBQ SFT+GRPO response length changes from 851.0 to 85.10 between v2 Table 9 and v4 Table 11. Section 4.5 swaps the placement of 2.44% and 19.73%, although Table 1 scores are unchanged. AIME results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The five theoretical derivations in Appendix A and mathematical definitions in Appendix F are retained. The new entropy-regularization discussion supplies a mechanism argument, not a new proof or formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: diversity-enhanced training for subjective reasoning, generalization to unseen subjective and objective tasks, and diversity as a stronger accuracy indicator than reasoning length. Headline gains of 14.1% and 7.64% are unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explicitly limits demonstrated applicability to existing multiple-choice benchmarks and discusses obstacles to free-form creative tasks. It also introduces an entropy-collapse mechanism argument. Section 5 and Appendix B add substantive explanations concerning filtering, perspective expansion, task-dependent diversity profiles, and possible overfitting of learned weights. These substantially expand the interpretation and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v4 substantially expands the previously sparse GRPO documentation: TRL implementation, 1,000 steps, AdamW, learning rate 5e-6, cosine scheduling, batch size 2, and prompt/completion limits of 2048/4096. Table 8 decomposes 2,700 SFT samples into 900 unique questions; validation counts and supervised-filtering details are newly disclosed. The code/data pointer changes from toward-agi/diverse-o1 to yumeng-10/multirole-r1.

R1.justification: v4 adds Cui et al. on entropy mechanisms and explicitly positions reward shaping against entropy regularization. It also adds citations to CostBench and NAACL. The broader related-work organization and claimed novelty of diversity-enhanced training for subjective questions remain intact.

P1.justification: v4 adds Discussion and Future Work before Related Work and Conclusion, with localized expansions of method and analysis explanations. It updates publication headers, adds an acknowledgment, and removes the author-contributions statement. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain.

P2.justification: v4 adds the opinion-count and training-composition tables and a six-panel subscore Figure 5, while extending existing tables with uncertainty and validation rows. Most displays retain their formats and are reflowed or renumbered. Figure 5 redisplays existing values but swaps function-word and n-gram labels in its ETHICS, CSQA, and GSM8K panels relative to Table 11.

improvement.justification: The expanded GRPO documentation, direct opinion-diversity analysis, human-rating variability, and explicit limits on free-form applicability make v4 easier to assess and reproduce while retaining the central empirical evidence. The gain is limited by introduced reporting errors: Section 4.5 swaps percentages despite unchanged benchmark scores, and Figure 5 mislabels two subscores in three panels.
